title: Estate Services Note: Conditions for an Estate Retirement Application (Capital Credits)
content:
# Conditions for an Estate Retirement Application

**Product:** Capital Credits (Patronage Capital). This note states when an application to retire a deceased member's capital credits for the estate may be taken, what makes it complete, and when it is approved.

## A. Who may apply

1. Estate retirement is offered only where the patron class allows it — every class except the Large Power Patron Class — only for an individual or joint membership, and only on the application of the person with authority over the deceased member's estate.
2. **Joint memberships.** For a joint membership (every class retires joint memberships for the estate only on the last death), the credits pass to the surviving joint member, and the estate application is taken only on the death of the last joint member, whose date of death is the date of death recorded on the member profile.

## B. Death on file

3. An estate application may be taken only when the member profile carries the date of death of a certified death certificate on file. The date recorded on the member profile is the authority; a caller's statement of the date does not replace it.

## C. Filing window

4. An estate application must be submitted within the class's estate claim window — 36 calendar months after the member's date of death in every class that offers estate retirement. Calendar months are counted from the date of death to the same day number of the later month, falling back to the last day of that month when the day number does not exist. An application submitted on the last day of the window is within it.
5. A late application leaves the credits in the general rotation.

| Date of death (hypothetical) | Last day of the 36-month window | Submitted | Within the window |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2023-05-31 | 2026-05-31 | 2026-05-31 | Yes — on the boundary day |
| 2023-05-31 | 2026-05-31 | 2026-06-01 | No — one day late |
| 2024-02-29 | 2027-02-28 (February 2027 has no 29th) | 2027-02-28 | Yes |
| 2024-02-29 | 2027-02-28 | 2027-03-01 | No |

## D. Complete application

6. The application is complete only when every required document is on file:
   - the certified death certificate;
   - an authority document of an accepted type — letters testamentary, letters of administration or a small estate affidavit — naming the claimant; and
   - the estate's IRS Form W-9, which every class requires.
7. A small estate affidavit is accepted only when the payout is at most the small estate affidavit limit, $25000.00.

| Death certificate | Authority document naming the claimant | Form W-9 | Complete |
|---|---|---|---|
| on file | letters testamentary | on file | Yes |
| on file | letters of administration | not on file | No |
| not on file | letters testamentary | on file | No |
| on file | small estate affidavit, payout $18,400.00 | on file | Yes |
| on file | small estate affidavit, payout $26,000.00 | on file | No |

## E. Approval

8. Complete applications are approved at the board meeting of the estate approval cycle — the monthly meeting on the third Tuesday. Whether an application is complete is read from the request record: the death certificate, the authority document type and the Form W-9 on file.

## F. Account status

Taking the application moves the deceased member's capital account, whether active or inactive, to estate claim pending, and records the date the application was submitted.
